shots.fallback: newborn face close up daylight indoors
shots.criteria: 6-12wk. Eyes open, converged above frame. Head bobble is a yes. REJECT sleeping baby, raised surface without a hand on them, propped bottle, any crib with bumpers/pillows/soft toys in background.

queries: baby locks eyes with mother close up
two month old baby face to face parent
shots.criteria: The gaze must ARRIVE, not already be parked. REJECT baby looking past/through. REJECT studio gloss.

queries: baby tracking parent face across room
shots.criteria: Eyes following, slow head turn ideal. No rolling, no reaching. REJECT tracking a TOY — the line is about faces.

queries: living room window daylight sofa lived in
shots.criteria: Real room, visible clutter is a plus. Cream and warm wood, daylight. REJECT cold north light, styled minimalism, ANY red in frame, any crib or sleep surface.

shots.fallback: parent talking to newborn face to face smiling
shots.criteria: HARDEST BEAT. Genuine social smile on a body that still reads 6-12wk. Judge by body not smile: fuller cheeks, steady head, teeth = too old. Fallback is parent smiling with baby three-quarter/back of head — the script says SOME babies smile back.

shots.fallback: baby mouth close up expression change
shots.criteria: Rounded vowel mouth, relaxed face. REJECT ANY crying or distressed baby — the line exists to distinguish these from crying. REJECT consonant babbling on an older baby.

shots.criteria: The WAITING must be visible — a clip with a natural pause beats a prettier one without. REJECT parent filming themselves or glancing at a phone.

shots.criteria: ONE baby, calm, unremarkable. TRAP: the line names two ages — NO split screen, NO two babies, NO timeline graphic, NO age labels. That is rule 5.
